item.title: Nagasaki Castella Cake — Guide
item.description: Castella (kasutera) is Nagasaki’s most famous sweet, a moist, fine-grained sponge cake with a springy texture and a rich, honeyed sweetness, baked in a distinctive tall loaf with a brown top and bottom crust and a sticky layer of sugar crystals at the base. It was introduced to Nagasaki by Portuguese merchants in the sixteenth century — its name comes from ‘bread of Castile’ — and over 400 years Japanese bakers refined the simple recipe of eggs, flour, sugar and starch syrup into the beloved cake it is today.
